symptom: ako/mxcli#859: under `mdl 1` an identical second exec of a `create or modify microflow|nanoflow` mxcli had just created was refused: 'a return is added where the stored flow does not end a path' (guard clause directly before the final return), 'the stored statement "Join" has no activity to address' (guard nested in an if without else), 'the Return at (x, y) is taken out' (nested guards on a wrapped row), 'the fragment returns' (two changes straddling a guard). Under mdl 0 the same re-run silently rebuilt the whole flow (MDL-V1-REBUILD). CapTrackV6: 36 refused statements in 12 of 35 scripts on pass 2.
cause: diff-then-patch matched the declared statements against describe's spelling of the stored graph, and describe spells several graphs differently from how authors write them: a split whose false flow goes straight to an end event is printed `if … else return … end if`; a nested guard sharing the outer merge is printed with a redundant `join shared1; merge shared1;`; a builder-wrapped row comes back as crossed-merge sections and an `elsif`. Unmatched, the statements became inserts/drops of returns the splice cannot make. The LCS also merged a changed statement before a guard with a change inside its then-branch into one replace whose fragment returned.
fix: planFlowModify first builds the declared flow as create would and compares it, read back through the codec (backend ReadBackMicroflow/ReadBackNanoflow: encode + decode, nothing written), with the stored graph up to element IDs (sameBuiltFlow: objects paired by position, flows by the objects they connect, every other property exact); the same graph means no body patch. For real edits, canonicalFlow rewrites both sides to one control-flow form (guard form for an if whose then-branch ends; a fall-through join+merge pair dropped) and lcsStatements pairs same-shell ifs so their branches are diffed separately.
insight: Matching two renderings of one graph is a losing game: every describe normalisation (#839 where/whitespace, #859 guards, joins, wrapped rows) is another spelling to reconcile, and the next one ships unseen because #850's parity property only runs describe's OWN spelling. Compare what the statement BUILDS with what is stored — the builder is deterministic, so an identical re-run is equal by construction, whatever describe prints. Read the built side back through the codec first: raw builder output differs from stored in writer defaults (a split's ErrorHandlingType Rollback vs unset). A property over AUTHORED scripts (TestFlowRerunProperty) is what sees this class; with the built comparison reverted it fails 68 mdl-examples scripts.
